claims.claim_text: We characterize the approaches by average distance travelled between infractions of five types: opposite lane, sidewalk, collision with static object, collision with car, and collision with pedestrian.
claims.normalized_text: Approaches are characterized by average distance between five types of infractions: opposite lane, sidewalk, collision with static object, collision with car, collision with pedestrian.

claims.claim_text: Opposite lane infraction is defined as more than 30% of the car’s footprint being over wrong-way lanes.
claims.normalized_text: Opposite lane infraction occurs when >30% of car footprint is over wrong-way lanes.

claims.claim_text: Sidewalk infraction is defined as more than 30% of the car’s footprint being over the sidewalk.
claims.normalized_text: Sidewalk infraction occurs when >30% of car footprint is over the sidewalk.

claims.claim_text: Collision with static object infraction is defined as the car making contact with a static object, such as a pole or building.
claims.normalized_text: Collision with static object infraction occurs when car contacts a static object like pole or building.

claims.claim_text: Collision with car infraction is defined as the car making contact with another car.
claims.normalized_text: Collision with car infraction occurs when car contacts another car.

claims.claim_text: Collision with pedestrian infraction is defined as the car making contact with a pedestrian.
claims.normalized_text: Collision with pedestrian infraction occurs when car contacts a pedestrian.

claims.claim_text: The duration of each violation is limited to 2 seconds, so if the car remains on the sidewalk for 10 seconds, this will be counted as 5 violations, not one.
claims.normalized_text: Each violation duration is capped at 2 seconds; a 10-second sidewalk stay counts as 5 violations.
